name: Sempan
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.note: 'Sempan is attested solely by the works of Drabbe'; lists Drabbe 1953 Kamoro grammar pp. 87-95 (discussion of Sempan) + pp. 96-104 (378-item list), Drabbe 1954, unpublished dictionary. Phonology paragraph: 10 consonants /m n p t k f h w r j/ and 5 vowels after Drabbe 1953:88, [h~s] varies by dialect. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pawley, A. & Hammarstrom, H. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In B. Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Documentation listing: 'Sempan [xse] 1,000 wordlist: Drabbe 1954a, 1950a, Galis 1955, Voorhoeve 1975b'. Nothing on Sempan stress.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1980. The Asmat languages of Irian Jaya. Pacific Linguistics B-64. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: 3.1.2.3 p. 22 and 7.2 p. 43: stress and pitch 'have only been studied to some extent in the KW dialect of CA and in CI'; Sempan appears only as comparative lexical evidence and a phonotactic note (p. 44: all Sempan words end in a vowel, /y/ or /w/). Nothing on Sempan stress. Bibliography lists Drabbe 1938 'Woordenboek van het Sempanees', mimeo.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 345-460. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 2.6.2.2.6.1.3 'Sempan' p. 372: sound system said to differ from Kamoro only in having fricatives h/s and f; nothing on stress. Sec. 2.6.2.2.6.1.2 'Kamoro' p. 370: 'Stress is indicated by Drabbe on individual words, but no rules of stress placement are given.' (second-hand, about Drabbe 1953).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Entry 36 SEMPAN (p. 31): villages Omawka, Moparawapi, Nateaymi, Farmapi, Otokwa; 'Sources: Drabbe 1953 (GN, Wl); Galis 1955 (N, Wl; S); U 1, 2' (U2 = Drabbe's unpublished Sempan-Dutch dictionary). No phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Greenhill, S. TransNewGuinea.org, 'Sempan' language page (lexical data from McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970, Voorhoeve 1975).
sources.note: 93 lexical items, no prosodic marking; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1968. The Central and South New Guinea Phylum. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 8 (Pacific Linguistics A-16), 1-18.
sources.note: Classification and lexicostatistics only ('Kamoro-Sempan-Asmat group (Drabbe 1953)'); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Drabbe, P. 1963. Drie Asmat-dialecten. Verhandelingen KITLV 42. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff.
sources.note: p. 2 fn. 1 points to the Sempan treatment in Spraakkunst van de Kamoro-Taal (KITLV 1953) 'randnummers 272-290, en de vergelijkende woordenlijst op bl. 96'. Its stress note (sec. 9, p. 13) covers Kawenak/Keenok/Keenakap Asmat only; nothing on Sempan stress.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, B. 2005. Asmat-Kamoro, Awyu-Dumut and Ok: an enquiry into their linguistic relationship. In Pawley et al. (eds), Papuan Pasts (Pacific Linguistics 572), 145-166. Canberra: ANU.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Latest comparative treatment using Drabbe's Sempan data (pp. 148-164); unlikely but possible remark on Asmat-Kamoro prosody

sources.citation: Drabbe, P. 1954. Talen en dialecten van Zuid-West Nieuw-Guinea. Micro-Bibliotheca Anthropos 11. Posieux/Fribourg: Institut Anthropos (microfilm); comparative 100-word vocabulary in 24 languages incl. Sémpan, pp. 230-257 (introductory instalment in Anthropos 45 (1950): 545-574, JSTOR).

sources.note: Drabbe's general remarks on the sound systems of the south-west New Guinea languages sometimes include a klemtoon note; the Sempan list is accent-marked.

sources.citation: Drabbe, P. 1953. Spraakkunst van de Kamoro-taal. 's-Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff (uitgave van het Koninklijk Instituut voor Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde). 111 pp. -- Sempan notes at marginal nos. 272-290 (pp. 87-95), Kamoro-Sempan-Asmat wordlist pp. 96-104, Kamoro phonology pp. 5 ff.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only
sources.note: The only first-hand description of Sempan (verb system compared with Kamoro, phoneme inventory p. 88) and the only place a Sempan stress remark or systematically accent-marked Sempan forms could exist; also needed for Kamoro [kgq]. Voorhoeve 1975 says Drabbe marks stress per word but gives no rule -- to be verified on the pages themselves.

sources.citation: Drabbe, P. 1938. Woordenboek van het Sempanees [Sempan-Dutch dictionary]. Mimeographed, unpublished (MSC mission archives; cited by Voorhoeve 1975 as unpublished source 2 and in Voorhoeve 1980 bibliography).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Drabbe's dictionaries carry accent marks on headwords; the distribution of marked stress across ~all Sempan lexemes would settle whether stress is fixed or lexical even without an explicit rule.
